standalone.identity: Benchmark verified embedded manifest binding; this CPU profile does not independently assert an archive digest.

method.scope: One main-thread V8 profile covering the complete diagnostic benchmark process, including fixture setup and cleanup.
method.weighting: Each leaf sample receives its matching timeDeltas entry in microseconds. Identical function/source/line frames are combined across calling contexts. Categories are exclusive self attribution, not inclusive stack totals.
method.nativeAttribution: Idle, program, and garbage collector samples are explicit categories. Node built-ins and application sources determine remaining categories. URL-less native frames inherit the closest recognizable ancestor category.
method.percentageDenominator: Sum of sampled timeDeltas, including idle time; these percentages are not whole-system CPU utilization.
method.sourceSanitization: Only node: built-ins and app/repository-relative source labels are emitted; unrecognized local locations become other-local-source.

interpretation.conclusion: This capture does not justify moving the application to Go or Rust. The main thread is predominantly idle, filesystem-related and process-launch frames dominate visible active categories, and application self frames are a small share of total sampled time.
observations: Idle is 77.588% of sampled elapsed time; filesystem-related frames are 9.291%, process-launch frames 3.294%, application frames 2.003%, and garbage collection 0.360%. The unresolved program category is 4.344%.

The largest aggregated named frame is Node child-process spawn at 540.472 ms. Native lstat is 477.574 ms, filesystem error handling 247.032 ms, and the JavaScript lstat wrapper 183.941 ms across the complete capture.
Largest application self frame is safePath at 61.032 ms (0.362%). Memory parsing/validation also appears, but the unprofiled 10,000-record search median is 31.0642 ms.

Unprofiled medians are 35.3027 ms CLI startup, 2631.8464 ms for synchronizing 1,000 files, and 503.6177 ms for the 300-file worktree diff. These motivate scoped investigation of file and process work, rather than establishing a language bottleneck.
nextMeasurements: Measure filesystem operation counts and latency within pack synchronization, especially repeated metadata probes and exception paths, while preserving path validation and transaction recovery guarantees.
Capture child Git/CLI startup and execution time plus Windows filesystem/worker activity before attributing parent idle samples to a particular cause.
Use allocation profiling and larger realistic memory datasets before treating process-cumulative RSS as an operation-specific memory problem.

Only compare a narrow Go or Rust worker after a remaining CPU-heavy hotspot and workload are isolated; compare end-to-end latency, memory, process startup, correctness, packaging, and cancellation under equivalent inputs.

limitations: The main-thread profile excludes CPU inside child Git and CLI processes, kernel work, and libuv worker threads. Their work may overlap parent idle samples.
V8 sampled elapsed attribution is not a direct measurement of CPU utilization. The program category is unresolved and must not be assigned to application JavaScript.
The capture includes benchmark setup and teardown; no phase markers were supplied, so category totals cannot be assigned exclusively to synchronization, search, or diff.
CPU profiling can add overhead. Instrumented versus baseline median differences are from separate short runs and include normal variability; they are not a controlled estimate of profiler overhead.
Seven startup samples and three heavy samples are insufficient for reliable tail-latency claims; reported p95 values reflect these small sample sets.
Synthetic temporary repositories and local files do not establish real developer workload performance, storage variability, concurrency behavior, or non-Windows performance.
No Go or Rust comparison was executed. Low garbage-collector sample share does not prove the absence of allocation or memory-pressure problems.
Raw profiler paths and contents were omitted from this public evidence artifact.
